pregnancy-placenta-12.title: Posterior placenta behind the fetus
pregnancy-placenta-12.label: Posterior placenta, 12 weeks 4 days
pregnancy-placenta-12.credit: Holly George et al., Fig. 1, Journal of Case Reports and Images in Obstetrics and Gynecology (2021)
pregnancy-placenta-12.reason: Compare the placental tissue along the far uterine wall with the adjacent fluid and fetus.
pregnancy-placenta-12.note: The authors describe a normal posterior placenta on this dating scan. The case later developed a placental complication. This image documents appearance at this visit. Fetal posture and image magnification differ, and the original CRL calipers belong to the acquired image. Complete published figure converted to lossless WebP.

pregnancy-placenta-48.title: Traced placental margin in a first-trimester ultrasound volume
pregnancy-placenta-48.label: Traced placental margin, different plane
pregnancy-placenta-48.credit: Victoria Melero-Jiménez et al., Fig. 1a, Children (2026)
pregnancy-placenta-48.reason: Follow the marked margin where placental tissue meets dark fluid.
pregnancy-placenta-48.note: Cropped the upper-left acquired view from the authors’ 3D ultrasound workstation in Fig. 1a. Orange points mark the contour, and color shows power Doppler. The highlighted placenta lies near the probe. The modeled transverse section shows a posterior placenta deeper in the field. The paper does not identify the maternal plane of this displayed slice. Color and tracing are preserved.

pregnancy-fetus-12.title: Fetal midsagittal profile at 12 weeks 2 days
pregnancy-fetus-12.label: Midsagittal profile, 12 weeks 2 days
pregnancy-fetus-12.credit: Maciej Korniluk et al., Fig. 1A, Journal of Clinical Medicine (2026)
pregnancy-fetus-12.reason: Follow the forehead, chin and trunk in the long section.
pregnancy-fetus-12.note: The acquired image displays 5.66 cm crown–rump length and 12 weeks 2 days. The model depicts a different fetal posture and a wider field. Original calipers and the panel letter are retained. Cropped panel A and resized for display.

pregnancy-fetus-48.title: Axial fetal head with paired choroid plexuses
pregnancy-fetus-48.label: Axial head with paired choroid plexuses
pregnancy-fetus-48.credit: Maciej Korniluk et al., Fig. 1D, Journal of Clinical Medicine (2026)
pregnancy-fetus-48.reason: Identify the two bright choroid plexuses and the skull outline in the transverse section.
pregnancy-fetus-48.note: The acquired head fills more of the display and is rotated in-plane relative to the model. The caption gives the study age range. The calipers on panel D belong to the published image. Cropped panel D and resized for display.
